title: Forecast-Dojo: Replayable Environments for Benchmarking and Training LLM Forecasting Agents
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 24 Sep 2026]
    Title:Forecast-Dojo: Replayable Environments for Benchmarking and Training LLM Forecasting Agents
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:We introduce Forecast-Dojo, a replayable environment for benchmarking and training LLM forecasting agents. It combines resolved prediction-market questions with dated news, allowing agents to research an event and revisit their predictions at successive historical dates. The same tasks and tools support repeated evaluation, collection of training interactions, and feedback from recorded outcomes without waiting for new events to resolve. Forecast-Dojo contains 1,568 Polymarket events, split by time into training and evaluation periods, and 18.8M dated news articles. In an evaluation of 12 models, research tools lower Brier score for all 12. Forecasts also improve as events unfold, with the largest gains at steps where more newly dated evidence is recorded. Every model still trails historical market forecasts in both Brier score and accuracy. A belief notebook carried between dates lowers research cost but does not consistently improve forecast quality. Beyond evaluation, Forecast-Dojo provides interaction trajectories and outcome feedback for agent learning, with supervised fine-tuning as a proof of concept.

report.summary: Forecast-Dojo offers replayable prediction-market environments and dated news to benchmark and train LLM forecasting agents, but models still trail market forecasts.
report.background: Forecasting future events is a long-standing test of reasoning under uncertainty. Prediction markets like Polymarket aggregate crowd wisdom into probabilities, while LLMs have recently been used as research assistants and autonomous forecasters. Existing benchmarks often rely on static question sets or live events, making repeated evaluation, training-data collection, and outcome feedback slow or non-reproducible. Forecast-Dojo addresses this by replaying resolved market questions at successive historical dates alongside contemporaneous news, so agents can research, revise, and be scored without waiting for real-world resolution. It sits at the intersection of agent evaluation, retrieval-augmented reasoning, and market-based forecasting.
key_points: Forecast-Dojo contains 1,568 Polymarket events split by time into training and evaluation periods, plus 18.8M dated news articles. This makes it a replayable testbed: agents see only news available at a given historical date and can revisit predictions as more evidence appears, enabling temporally honest evaluation and training without waiting for new events.

In an evaluation of 12 models, research tools lower Brier score for all 12. Forecasts also improve as events unfold, with the largest gains at steps where more newly dated evidence is recorded. Every model still trails historical market forecasts in both Brier score and accuracy.

A belief notebook carried between dates lowers research cost but does not consistently improve forecast quality. This suggests memory and state can reduce token or tool use, yet effective forecasting depends more on evidence selection and calibration than on simply retaining prior beliefs.

Beyond evaluation, Forecast-Dojo provides interaction trajectories and recorded outcomes for agent learning, with supervised fine-tuning as a proof of concept. The paper positions this as a bridge from static benchmarking to iterative agent improvement using replayable historical feedback.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Forecast-Dojo shifts forecasting benchmarks from static Q&A toward replayable, temporally grounded agent evaluations. It gives a reproducible way to compare retrieval, memory, and calibration strategies, and shows a gap remains between LLM agents and prediction markets. Developers can use the environment to train or evaluate forecasting agents with outcome feedback, and tools like belief notebooks highlight cost/quality trade-offs. Regular users should be cautious: LLM forecasts improved with research and unfolding news, but they still underperformed market benchmarks, so they are better treated as analytical aids than reliable oracles. It also creates a reusable pipeline for generating interaction trajectories, which could accelerate agent post-training and evaluation standards across domains beyond forecasting.
report.tools: Follow the arXiv paper and any linked code or data. Related tools: Polymarket API for prediction-market questions and prices; Hugging Face Datasets for hosting news and question corpora; LangChain or LlamaIndex for retrieval over dated news; AutoGen, CrewAI, or OpenAI Agents SDK for multi-step forecasting agents; Inspect or OpenAI Evals for benchmarking; scikit-learn or custom scripts for Brier score. Watch for open-source replication of Forecast-Dojo's replay harness.
